thesis_he.bear: הביקוש לענן AI ממשיך, אבל המחיר לשעת GPU יורד, ההייפרסקיילרים ו-CoreWeave לוקחים את החוזים הגדולים, והמימון היקר והדילול אוכלים את הצמיחה; לנביוס אין חפיר שמגן על התשואה.
thesis_he.base: המחסור בכוח חשמל מחובר וב-GPU נמשך עד 2027, נביוס ממירה חלק גדול מהחשמל החוזי לקיבולת פעילה ומוכרת אותה בחוזים ארוכים עם תשלום מראש, וצומחת מהר יותר מ-CoreWeave מבסיס קטן, אבל נשארת תלויה בכמה לקוחות גדולים ובמימון חיצוני.
thesis_he.bull: נביוס מחברת 800-1000 מגה-וואט עד סוף 2026 ותוכנית של יותר מגיגה-וואט ב-2027, ממלאת אותם בחוזים של 20-25 מיליון דולר למגה-וואט בשנה, והשכבה התוכנתית (Token Factory) מחזיקה מחיר גבוה גם כשהשוק עובר להסקה.

market_direction.reading: Demand for contracted AI compute is rising on the buyers' own commitments, not logos: NBIS RPO was $37.5B at 2026-06-30 (36% due within 24 months) and management cites more than $40B of contracted backlog incl. investment-grade long-term deals; named competitor CoreWeave's RPO rose from $60.7B (2025-12-31) to $103.7B (2026-06-30). Management says it could sell all 2027 capacity on landmark-deal terms. Counter-signals at as_of: press reports a Gartner warning (14 Oct 2026) that more than 80% of neoclouds may not stay independent by 2030 and a neocloud credit sell-off (secondary press, the report itself not read).

bottleneck_potential.reading: NBIS is not itself a bottleneck: it buys the scarce inputs (powered, connected data-center capacity and NVIDIA GPUs from three suppliers that carried Q2 capex). Its edge is holding scarce capacity: about 170 MW active at end-2025, more than 2 GW contracted (Feb 2026), guidance of 800-1000 MW connected and 5 GW contracted by end-2026. The window lasts while connected power is short; capacity adders are CoreWeave, Crusoe, Lambda, the hyperscalers and state programmes (20-F). How long the shortage lasts is not independently evidenced.

share_trajectory.reading: NBIS is gaining relative to named competitor CoreWeave in reported revenue, from a much smaller base: Nebius AI cloud revenue $574.9M in Q2 2026 vs $93.7M in Q2 2025 (about 6.1x), group $582.3M vs $105.1M (5.5x), against CoreWeave $2,575M vs $1,212M (2.1x); NBIS is about 22.6% of CoreWeave's quarterly revenue (derived). ARR rose from $1.9B (2026-03-31) to $3.0B (2026-06-30). No measured market-share figure and no numbers for Crusoe, Lambda or Oracle's AI cloud, so share against the full named set is a gap.

competitive_position.reading: Against CoreWeave: smaller (RPO $37.5B vs $103.7B; quarterly revenue about a quarter) and less profitable on GAAP (Q2 2026 operating margin about -30% vs about -2%, derived), but its AI cloud segment shows a 50% adjusted EBITDA margin and customer prepayments fund about 55% of the associated capex on Q2 deals, with $8.0B cash at 2026-06-30. Pricing signal: first capacity auction cleared 15% above the highest Blackwell price charged before, and short-term capacity sells at $40-50M per MW-year vs $20-25M on long deals (management). Against hyperscalers (AWS, Google, Azure, Oracle): weaker on scale and cost of capital; differentiation is the full-stack software and inference layer (Token Factory, Inferize acquisition). Crusoe and Lambda: no numbers (private).

threats.reading: 1) Pricing: the 20-F expects increasing competition to press prices; NBIS launched public spot pricing and auctions (Oct 2026), which also exposes it to spot-price declines. 2) In-sourcing/substitution: the largest buyers (Microsoft, Meta, with Microsoft TCV up to about $17.4B through 2031) build their own capacity; the 20-F flags AI models needing less compute. 3) Financing: capital-bound build-out (2026 capex guide $20-25B) funded by converts, ATM equity, prefunded warrants and a 364-day $3.5B Citi facility at SOFR+2.75%: a credit-market shut-off slows growth (neocloud sell-off Oct 2026, press). 4) Regulation: BIS export-control policy on advanced computing and a proposed IaaS KYC rule; rising US scrutiny of data-center power demand.

moat.note: No durable moat source evidenced against CoreWeave or the hyperscalers: the product (GPU capacity) is bought from the same suppliers; ROIC last -8.7% and incremental ROIC -45% (forensic screen). Current advantage is scarce powered capacity and contracts, which competitors are adding too; returns should fade toward the cost of capital unless the software layer proves pricing.

switching_costs.note: Multi-year take-or-pay contracts (Meta, Microsoft, Q2 landmark deals with 50-60% upfront payments) lock in revenue for their terms (RPO $37.5B, 64% beyond 24 months); but the 20-F says most other engagements are short-term, and customers carry termination rights on delivery delays.

pricing_power.note: Auction cleared 15% above the prior Blackwell high and short-term capacity sells at $40-50M per MW-year vs $20-25M on long deals (management statements); the 20-F itself expects competition to press prices. Evidence is of a shortage price, not of durable power versus CoreWeave.

customer_concentration.note: Three unnamed customers were 24%, 21% and 14% of Q2 2026 revenue (59% together); Microsoft and Meta contracts are large relative to revenue; losing or delaying one tranche moves revenue materially.

market_size.note: Contracted demand across NBIS ($37.5B RPO, more than $40B backlog per management) and CoreWeave ($103.7B RPO) is many times NBIS's current revenue; no attributed independent market-size study was read (gap).

competition.note: Named rivals CoreWeave (about 4x NBIS revenue, 2.8x RPO), Crusoe, Lambda and AWS/Google/Azure/Oracle compete for the same AI-lab and hyperscaler contracts; Token Factory faces Fireworks AI and Together AI.

substitutes.note: Main substitutes are hyperscaler in-house capacity and more compute-efficient models (20-F risk); not sized. Current hyperscaler contracts with NBIS show buyers still renting capacity.

management.note: Executed the 2024 divestiture of all Russian businesses and the pivot to AI cloud; ARR grew from $1.9B to $3.0B in one quarter and 2026 guidance was reaffirmed on 2026-08-12. Guidance track record not computed (gap); implied H2 2026 revenue of $2.0-2.4B vs H1 $0.98B is a steep ramp still to be proven (Q3 results 2026-11-12).

capital_allocation.note: H1 2026 funding via $4.34B converts, $2.85B treasury share sales and $2.0B prefunded warrants to NVIDIA, 12.7M ATM shares in Q2, a further $4.5B convert offering (Aug) and a 364-day Citi facility: heavy current-holder dilution and refinancing risk; incremental ROIC -45%. Offset: customer prepayments cover about 55% of associated capex on Q2 deals.

governance.note: Dual-class structure (238.4M Class A, 33.5M Class B at 2026-06-30); votes per Class B share and control holders not read in this part (gap).

regulation.note: Export controls on advanced computing and a proposed BIS IaaS KYC rule; US scrutiny of data-center power use and local site approvals (Vineland NJ hearing adjourned). Non-US customers about 36% of FY2025 revenue is an upper bound, not an evidenced loss.

technology_ai.note: AI cloud segment adjusted EBITDA margin 50% in Q2 2026, Vera Rubin deployment expected late 2026/early 2027, inference stack built through Inferize and Eigen AI acquisitions; no evidence yet that the software layer earns a price premium over CoreWeave.

geopolitics.note: Revenue 64% US-located (FY2025); Israel 4.3% of long-lived assets (US-Israel-Iran hostilities risk); Russian businesses fully divested in 2024 with no Russian customers or suppliers per the 20-F; GPU supply exposed to tariffs and export controls (unsized).

gaps: Outside view (warning only, moves no number): very high revenue-growth expectations are rarely sustained across five years and capital-intensive neoclouds face a consolidation warning (Gartner, secondary press); no base rate was applied.
Crusoe and Lambda are private: no numbers; Oracle and AWS/Google/Azure AI-cloud revenue not collected, so share against the full named set is not measurable.
